issues.legal_issue: A transfer made before evacuee-property restrictions apply may be refused confirmation for lack of good faith when the transferor deliberately makes it to defeat the anticipated application of those restrictions.
material_facts: The transferor had left India and settled in Pakistan and sought to convert property in India into cash to take to Pakistan.

The transferor’s letter expressed concern that delay would bring new government rules, and the authorities found that he hurried the sale to evade the anticipated extension of evacuee-property restrictions.
The sale was completed before those restrictions had been extended to the relevant territory.
The purchaser paid valuable consideration and was not shown to have acted in bad faith.
issues.conclusion: The transferor’s deliberate intention to defeat the anticipated application of evacuee-property restrictions was inconsistent with good faith under the statutory confirmation scheme. The authorities could therefore refuse confirmation, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 40(1) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, transfers within its scope required confirmation to confer rights; section 40(4)(a) permitted rejection where a transaction was not entered into in good faith or for valuable consideration. Good faith under section 3(22) of the General Clauses Act ordinarily concerns honesty, but that definition applies unless repugnant to the subject or context. Read in light of section 40’s purpose of preserving evacuee property, a deliberate transfer intended to defeat restrictions known to be imminent is not in good faith, even if those restrictions had not yet been extended to the territory. Good faith is required of both transferor and transferee; the transferee’s good faith and payment of consideration do not cure the transferor’s lack of good faith. The Court distinguished the protection for a good-faith transferee under section 53(1) of the Transfer of Property Act. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_confirmation_refusal: A party appealed the refusal to confirm a transfer under a statutory scheme governing transfers of evacuee property.
predicates.transferor_knew_restrictions_were_immine: The transferor knew that restrictions on dealing with the property were likely to be applied soon.
predicates.transferor_sold_solely_to_evade_restrict: The transferor made the transfer solely to defeat the anticipated application of those restrictions.

issues.definition: When a refusal-of-confirmation appeal involves a transferor who knew restrictions were imminent and transferred solely to evade them, the transfer lacks good faith and confirmation may be refused.
